notes.summary: Proved ordinary-test bipolar and finite-test criteria for positive doubly closed exhaustion on one fixed neighborhood. Constructed-current density remains unproved; no analytic counterexample results.
notes.detailedSummary: On a fixed ordinary neighborhood N, let E be the actual complementary compact smooth symmetric test space, P its middle-positive cone, and B the symmetric projections of both first differential images. The allowed current cone C is the nonnegative annihilator of P+B, and its test polar is H=closure(P+B) in the weak topology induced by ordinary currents. For an actual construction cone G contained in C, an allowed T is weakly approximable by G exactly when every finite full-test list admits an actual candidate on the same N, or equivalently T is nonnegative on G*. Every current in C is exhausted exactly when G*=H. These equivalences preserve all analytic-unit refinements but establish neither feasibility nor density.
notes.text:
This is a proved reduction, not a resolution of P21.3. Retain every original complete non-Archimedean field, including trivial valuation, the good separated strict boundaryless pure n-dimensional analytic space, n>=2, one fixed ordinary neighborhood N, and every p=0,...,n-1. Put q=n-p>=1. Currents use the original canonical calibration and actual generic lengths, including singularities and nilpotents.

The external ordinary-calculus premises are CLD arXiv:1204.6277v2, 25 July 2025, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2: 11.1.7 and 15.7.1-2 give ordinary analytic opens and canonical restriction; 15.2.2-9 give local differential separation, compact cutoffs and smooth scalar density; 7.1.1-7 give continuous current duals, evaluation topology, restriction and sheaf; 6.5.2 and 7.2.1-4 give compact symmetric-test decomposition into middle-positive tests and middle positivity; 7.7.1-5 give both differential dualities. Their hypotheses apply on the original ordinary opens over either valuation regime, with no global paracompactness needed for compact-support assertions. The explicitly supplied reviewed core supplies its middle-cone multiplication arguments and precisely Theorem 3's compatible-current operations. No density or reverse recognition is granted. There are no supplied canonical note IDs.

Define E=A_c^(q,q)(N)_sym, F=D^(p,p)(N)_sym using actual ordinary continuous currents, and Pi as symmetric projection. Let P be the middle-positive test cone and
B={Pi(d'psi+d''chi): psi in A_c^(q-1,q)(N), chi in A_c^(q,q-1)(N)}.
Let C={T in F: T>=0, d'T=d''T=0}, and H=closure(P+B) for sigma(E,F). Then
C={T: T(P)>=0, T(B)=0},
H={beta: T(beta)>=0 for every T in C}.
The first equality checks the two differential equations separately by duality.

Here is the separation proof needed for the second equality. For paired vector spaces V,V' with the weak testing topology and a convex cone A containing zero, v outside closure(A) has a finite test-coordinate map e such that t=e(v) lies outside L=closure(e(A)) in R^m. A nearest point z in the closed convex cone L exists using a bounded minimizing sequence. Minimality along segments gives (t-z).(y-z)<=0. Taking y=0 and 2z gives (t-z).z=0. Thus a=z-t satisfies a.y>=0 on L and a.t=-||t-z||^2<0. The corresponding finite combination of testing functionals separates v from A. This works even with a kernel in the pairing.

Apply this to P+B. A separator is a finite combination of ordinary continuous currents, hence an actual ordinary current R. Nonnegativity on P gives middle positivity. Since both b and -b belong to P+B, R annihilates B and satisfies both closedness equations. Thus R belongs to C. Conversely every member of C is nonnegative on P+B and its weak closure. This proves the claimed bipolar identity without extending a functional from one moment chart.

Let G be any cone of actual allowed currents on all of N, closed under addition and nonnegative scaling. In particular use the precise system generated from delta_X by the supplied Theorem 3 operations: restriction, agreeing gluing, permitted smooth positive doubly closed factors, permitted D(vS), and fixed-degree weak positive limits that are actual currents. Put G*={beta: S(beta)>=0 for all S in G}. For T in C, weak membership in closure(G) is equivalent to: every finite L subset E and epsilon>0 admit a single S in G on all N with |(S-T)(beta)|<epsilon for beta in L. The same separation argument with the paired spaces reversed makes this equivalent to T being nonnegative on G*.

Finite feasibility supplies a genuine net indexed by finite test sets L and positive integers m, ordered by inclusion and increasing m, choosing error<1/m. Every fixed test is eventually controlled. Every term must already be an actual positive doubly closed current on the same N, including compatibility with refinements outside the finite list. Finite constraints do not certify an analytic current. Consequently all C are exhausted exactly when G*=H: H is always contained in G*; equality gives exhaustion, while exhaustion makes every G*-test nonnegative on C and therefore in H.

All compact ordinary tests, and hence all analytic-unit moment refinements, occur in the directed set. N never shrinks with the index. Smooth localization can decompose tests; it does not glue unrelated approximating currents.

For positive R and beta=eta_1-eta_2 with compact positive eta_i, set eta=eta_1+eta_2. The supplied coefficient-measure calculus gives |<bR,beta>|<=||b||_supp(eta)<R,eta> for continuous b. Smooth scalar approximation and eventual bounds on positive tested masses prove bS_a->bT for positive weak nets. Thus exhaustion by compatible G would imply D((U-V)T)=0, followed by ordinary sheaf locality on the pair's domain.

Neither finite feasibility nor G*=H is proved near arbitrary analytic germs. An exhaustion separator need not equal a multiplier detector hD(alpha), and supplies neither an admissible pair nor canonical upstairs Hessian equality. It is not a P21.3 counterexample.

The selected primary search inspected CLD Euclidean convolution, GR real-PL recognition, toric Lagerberg products and Jell smooth Poincare statements. Their domains do not supply the missing arbitrary analytic-current construction. The BGJKK PDF inspected was the identified 2021 v1 preprint; its 2025 published revision was not audited.

Deliverables are P21.3-paper.tex, P21.3-paper.pdf and P21.3-argument.md, with literal primary evidence, premises.json, source-manifest.json, literature-bindings.json and the exact five-field status.json. Original input-original.json, task-original.json and assignment-original.txt are preserved. Run bash reproduce.sh in the deliverable directory. The nine-page PDF builds successfully. Integrity checks pass for frozen inputs, 29 literal CLD slices, six source-URL-selected web units and two backward-supported notes. These finite execution checks are not mathematical audits. No heavy compute facility was supplied or launched. Original P21.3 remains unresolved.

notes.summary: Proved an exact compact-mass scalar criterion and sufficient test certificates for arbitrary-current relation preservation. Canonical Hessian equality does not yet yield these certificates or zero defect.
notes.detailedSummary: Using n1's ordinary test bipolar cone H, fix beta=D alpha=eta_1-eta_2 and eta=eta_1+eta_2. The supremum Lambda_eta(h;alpha) of |<hT,D alpha>| over allowed currents with T(eta)<=1 is finite, uniformly stable in h, and zero exactly when all unnormalized pairings vanish. For smooth g it equals inf{a>=0: a eta +/- g D alpha belong to H}. Smooth scalar approximation makes these infima converge to Lambda with the uniform approximation error. Positive-plus-both-first-exact compact test certificates with coefficients tending to zero therefore suffice for arbitrary-current independence. Their existence from D[h]=0 is unproved, and no positive-defect admissible pair is exhibited.
notes.text:
This note uses n1's ordinary test bipolar identity and its stated calculus premises. It retains all original fields, analytic hypotheses, degrees, singularities, nilpotents and canonical lengths. It assumes no constructed-current density.

Fix a compact symmetric alpha of type (q-1,q-1) on the same ordinary N and put beta=D alpha, D=d'd''. Since DJ=JD, beta is symmetric. Choose compact middle-positive eta_1,eta_2 with beta=eta_1-eta_2; set eta=eta_1+eta_2 and K_eta=supp eta. This compact support may exceed supp beta. For continuous real h define
L_(h,alpha)(T)=<hT,beta>=<D(hT),alpha>,
Lambda_eta(h;alpha)=sup{|L_(h,alpha)(T)|: T in C, <T,eta><=1}.
The supremum uses actual ordinary analytic currents. No attainment or compactness of this current family is assumed.

The coefficient-measure bound in n1 proves Lambda_eta(h;alpha)<=||h||_K_eta and
|Lambda_eta(h;alpha)-Lambda_eta(k;alpha)|<=||h-k||_K_eta.
If <T,eta>=0, the same bound already forces L(T)=0. Otherwise normalize T by its positive mass. Therefore Lambda=0 exactly when L vanishes for every T in C. No zero mass is divided by.

For a smooth real scalar g on N define
a_eta(g;alpha)=inf{a>=0: a eta+g beta in H and a eta-g beta in H}.
This is finite: with M=||g||_K_eta, the tests M eta +/- g beta equal (M+/-g)eta_1+(M-/+g)eta_2 and are positive wherever their factors are nonzero. No psh or harmonic property of g is required.

By n1's bipolar identity, the two H-memberships are equivalent to |<T,g beta>|<=a<T,eta> for every T in C. Smooth multiplication identifies the pairing with L_(g,alpha)(T). Normalizing positive-mass currents and treating zero mass separately proves
a_eta(g;alpha)=Lambda_eta(g;alpha).
The permitted a form a closed ray because H is weakly closed.

CLD v2 15.2.5-7 gives compact smooth scalars g_j on N with epsilon_j=||g_j-h||_K_eta->0: first multiply h by a compact cutoff equal to one near K_eta, then approximate the resulting compact continuous function. Uniform stability proves
|a_eta(g_j;alpha)-Lambda_eta(h;alpha)|<=epsilon_j.
Hence D(hT)=0 for every T in C exactly when these infima tend to zero for every alpha, for one or every such scalar approximation. Symmetric detectors suffice because hT and D(hT) are symmetric. The numerical supremum can depend on the positive decomposition, but its zero condition is independent because it expresses the same unnormalized vanishing against all T.

A concrete sufficient certificate is the following. For each alpha, suppose smooth g_j on this fixed N, nonnegative a_j->0, compact positive xi_j^+/- and compact psi_j^+/- of type (q-1,q), chi_j^+/- of type (q,q-1) satisfy
a_j eta +/- g_j D alpha = xi_j^+/- + Pi(d'psi_j^+/- + d''chi_j^+/-),
||g_j-h||_K_eta->0.
Evaluation on arbitrary T in C kills each first differential term separately and is nonnegative on xi. Thus |<T,g_j D alpha>|<=a_j<T,eta>. Adding the scalar error estimate and passing to the limit gives <hT,D alpha>=0. Testing every alpha proves D(hT)=0. Membership of the left sides in H instead of P+B also suffices by the bipolar identity; the limiting-infimum criterion is exact. All functions and forms remain on the same N and respect their analytic moment refinements.

For an original separately admissible continuous generated-Psh pair h=U-V, canonical upstairs equality D[h]=0 gives only L_(h,alpha)(delta_X|N)=0 for all alpha. It does not bound the supremum over arbitrary allowed currents or construct the certificates. Proving this control is the remaining geometric relation-preservation step. Neither it nor generated-Psh membership of both signs of h is established here.

If Lambda were positive for an actual admissible pair and compact alpha, its definition would yield an actual allowed T with nonzero Hessian pairing without requiring attainment. No such pair, value, current or detector is exhibited. This reduction is therefore neither an analytic counterexample nor a solution of the original every-open assertion.
